instruction: Translate the foreign-language literature in PDF format into Chinese and place the translation in a new Word document. Also place the images from the PDF at appropriate locations in the Word document, and format the new Word document according to the document “002 Graduation Project Foreign-Language Translation Cover and Formatting Requirements (Regular Class).”

dim1: The deliverable is in .docx format and can be opened normally.
dim2: +5: All text in the document is in Chinese except for the content below “References.”
+1: Page 1 cover main title: the text “Graduation Project (Thesis)” uses the Microsoft YaHei font in Chuhao size.
+1: Page 1 cover main title: leave four blank lines before the text “Graduation Project (Thesis)”; center-align it and use single line spacing.

+1: On the first page, “Foreign-Language Translation” uses the DengXian font in Erhao size and bold, with the text centered and arranged vertically, positioned approximately one-quarter of the way down from the top of the page below the text “Graduation Project (Thesis),” with single line spacing.
+1: On page 1, the title is “Design and Evaluation of a Community Reading Garden Project for Intergenerational Learning,” in SimSun, Sanhao size, with single line spacing and justified alignment.

+3: Page 1 cover personal-information table: place fields such as Major, Class, Student Name, Student ID, and Advisor, along with their completed entries, in a table below the text “Foreign-Language Translation,” with each item on a separate row and centered. The table has 7 rows and 2 columns; the first column is 2.65 cm wide, the second column is 7.86 cm wide, and all rows have a uniform height of 2.65 cm.

+3: Page 1 cover personal-information area: fields such as Major, Class, Student Name, Student ID, and Advisor use bold SimSun in Sanhao size with distributed alignment; their completed entries use SimSun in Sanhao size, are center-aligned, and remain editable.

+1: Institution/year page: include an image 6-8 cm wide and 2-4 cm high and the text “Year 2026” in SimSun, Sanhao size. Place the image above the text “Year 2026,” centered at the bottom of the cover page.

+1: Chinese main-text title: the translated Chinese title appears at the top of the first page of the main text, in SimHei, Erhao size, horizontally centered, with 0.5 lines of spacing before and 0.5 lines after.

+1: Abstract heading and body: “【Abstract】” and the complete Chinese abstract are present, using Wuhao size; Chinese text uses SimSun, while English text and numbers use Times New Roman. Leave one blank line after the final paragraph of the abstract.

+1: Keywords section: below the abstract, include “Keywords: Reading Garden，Community Learning，Family Literacy，Outdoor Library，Participatory Evaluation” or five Chinese keywords with accurately equivalent meanings, separated by Chinese commas. The keywords use SimSun in Wuhao size; the three characters “Keywords” use bold SimSun in Wuhao size; English text and numbers use Times New Roman. Leave one blank line after the keywords paragraph.

+5: Primary heading format: all primary headings from Chapter 1 through Chapter 13 use “SimHei in Sanhao size, left alignment, 1 line of spacing before, 1 line after, and single line spacing,” with 1 character space between the heading number and heading text.

+5: Secondary heading format: secondary headings use numbering such as 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, and 3.2. They use SimHei in Xiaosan size, with English text and numbers in Times New Roman, justified alignment, 0.5 lines of spacing before, 0.5 lines after, 1 space between the section number and section title text, and single line spacing; “Snap to grid when document grid is defined” is selected.

+5: Main-text paragraph format: Chinese body text consistently uses SimSun in Xiaosi size; English text, numbers, and Western punctuation use Times New Roman in Xiaosi size; Greek letters or special symbols use the Symbol font. Regular body paragraphs have a first-line indent of 0.85 cm or two full-width characters, use single line spacing, and have “Snap to grid when document grid is defined” selected. The Chinese translation uses full-width Chinese punctuation, while English abbreviations, numbers, terms such as SLAM, and similar content use half-width characters. Figure numbers, table numbers, and chapter numbering remain consistent.

+5: Throughout the document, the Chinese text of figure captions and table captions uses SimSun in Wuhao size; the numerals in figure and table numbers use Times New Roman in Wuhao size; all are center-aligned.

+1: Figure 1, Reading Garden Service Flowchart: insert it after the relevant paragraph in Chapter 1, “Background and Purpose,” and before or near Section 1.1, at 9-11 cm wide and 5-8 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 1 Service Logic of the Reading Garden Project” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+1: Figure 2, Temporary Reading Garden Diagram: insert it near Chapter 2, “Collection Strategy,” at 9-11 cm wide and 5-8 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 2 Original Vector Diagram of the Temporary Reading Garden” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+1: Figure 3, Observation Zones and Movement Paths Diagram: insert it near “Observation Plan” or “Reliability Check” in Chapter 3, at 9-11 cm wide and 5-8 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 3 Observation Areas and Participant Movement Paths Used by Staff in the Project.” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+1: Figure 4, Twelve-Week Participation Trend Chart: insert it near the discussion of participation and usage patterns in Chapter 4, at 9-11 cm wide and 5-8 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 4 Participation Records over the Twelve-Week Period, Combining Youth Visits, Adult Visits, and the Percentage of Returning Families.” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+1: Figure 5, Multi-Metric Results Chart: insert it between Chapter 6, Operational Findings, and Chapter 7, Learning Outcomes, or near the corresponding analysis paragraph, at 14-16 cm wide and 10-12 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 5 Multi-Metric Results Used to Guide Weekly Adjustments.” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+1: Figure 6, Portable Resource Toolkit Image: insert it near the content related to family participation in Chapter 7, at 9-11 cm wide and 5-8 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 6 Portable Toolkit Used to Assemble the Project, Showing the Relationship Between Movable Resources and the Activity Process” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+1: Figure 7, Twelve-Week Implementation Matrix: insert it near “Implementation Matrix” in Chapter 9, at 9-11 cm wide and 5-8 cm high. Below the image, include the Chinese figure caption “Figure 7 Implementation Matrix for Use by Libraries or Schools When Adapting the Project” or a Chinese caption with accurately equivalent meaning.

+3: Table 1, Project Components Table: create an editable Word table at the corresponding location in Chapter 2, including columns such as “Component,” “Primary Function,” and “Evidence Source,” and translate content such as mobile book crates, shade canopies, quiet cushions, prompt cards, recording boxes, and garden labels.

+3: Table 2, Twelve-Week Activity Cycle Table: create an editable table at the corresponding location in Chapter 4, including Week, Theme, Youth Visits, Adult Visits, Return Rate, Staff Minutes, and Adjustments, retaining all 12 weeks of data.

+3: Table 3, Average Workload Table: create an editable table at the corresponding location in Chapter 6, including rows such as Site Setup, Greeting, Materials Maintenance, Observation Records, Closing Cleanup, and Total, and columns such as Weeks 1—3, Weeks 4—8, and Weeks 9—12.

+3: Table 4, Design Trade-Offs Table: create an editable table at the corresponding location in Chapter 8, including columns such as Trade-Off, Risk of Neglect, and Operational Response; the table text has been translated into Chinese.

+3: Table 5, Transfer Guide Table: create an editable table at the end of Chapter 12 or before Chapter 13, including columns such as Planning Area, Minimum Action, Improvement Action After the Pilot, and Review Point.
+1: Odd-page headers in the main text: odd pages in the main text display “Foreign-Language Translation” in the header, using SimSun in Xiaowu size and centered in the header.

+1: Even-page headers in the main text: even pages in the main text display “Class of 2022 Materials Science and Engineering Graduation Project (Thesis)” in the header, using SimSun in Xiaowu size and centered in the header.

+1: Main-text page numbers: beginning with the first page of the translated main-text abstract, use consecutive Arabic page numbers starting at 1, centered in the footer. Do not display main-text page numbers on the cover or institution/year page.
+1: Page setup: the main-text pages are A4 in portrait orientation, with 2.5 cm margins on the top, bottom, left, and right; the header distance is 1.5 cm and the footer distance is 1.5 cm.

+1: References section: the heading “References (Omitted; Not Translated)” or “References” appears at the end of the main text and uses the primary heading format. Do not translate the English references; the references must not be incorrectly translated as Chinese body text.
